## Release Cadence

SQLModel has been in active development since 2021 but remains on 0.0.x
versioning after 4+ years [14][19]. Key releases:

| Version | Date | Significance |
|---|---|---|
| 0.0.37 | Feb 2026 | Build CI fix |
| 0.0.35 | 2025 | Dropped Python 3.9 |
| 0.0.32 | 2025 | Fixed Pydantic 2.12+ Annotated compatibility |
| 0.0.31 | 2025 | BREAKING: Removed Pydantic v1 support |
| 0.0.27 | 2024 | Added Python 3.14 support |
| 0.0.24 | 2024 | Added Python 3.13 support |
| 0.0.21 | 2024 | Cascade delete relationships |
| 0.0.20 | 2024 | Official UUID support |
| 0.0.14 | Dec 2023 | Full Pydantic v2 support |
| 0.0.12 | 2023 | SQLAlchemy 2.0 upgrade |

## Maintenance Philosophy

Tiangolo (October 2023 roadmap) [11]:

> "Work on SQLModel is alternated (and sometimes mixed) with work on Typer,
> SQLModel, Asyncer, and others."

Main maintenance activities described as "answering questions and reviewing
pull requests" [11]. No strict definition of "maintenance" offered [11].

## Historical Concerns

In August 2022, community concern peaked when version 0.0.6 had been stagnant
for over a year [10]. Key complaints:

- UUID support missing (issue #25) [10]
- Pinned to outdated SQLAlchemy versions [10]
- Enum workarounds required [10]
- "Those problems have proposed solutions and open Pull Requests, but they
  are neither reviewed nor merged" [10]

**Resolution:** Most of these specific issues were addressed in subsequent
releases — UUID in 0.0.20, SQLAlchemy 2.0 in 0.0.12, Pydantic v2 in
0.0.14 [14].

## Community Sentiment

**Positive signals:**
- 17.8k stars indicates strong community interest [19]
- Active issue tracker with recent discussions [19]
- Articles in 2025 still discussing SQLModel as viable [18]
- Sponsored by GOVCERT.LU [19]

**Negative signals:**
- Still 0.0.x after 4+ years — no stable 1.0 release [14]
- Single maintainer across multiple projects [11]
- Some community members concluded they'd avoid SQLModel [11]
- Periodic cycles of concern about maintenance velocity [10]

## Gaps and Limitations

- The 0.0.x versioning provides no semantic versioning guarantees — breaking
  changes have occurred in minor versions (0.0.31, 0.0.35) [14]
- Single-maintainer risk remains the primary sustainability concern
- Several roadmap items from October 2023 remain pending as of April 2026
